claims.statement: `build_server()` registers exactly seven read tools unconditionally and registers `commit_note` only inside an `if write_enabled:` branch, so a read-only server is read-only structurally: no write tool exists to be talked into a write.

The registered tool names are published as data in `READ_TOOL_NAMES` and `WRITE_TOOL_NAMES`, and the test suite asserts the live registration set equals exactly `READ_TOOL_NAMES` on a read-only server and `READ_TOOL_NAMES | WRITE_TOOL_NAMES` on a write-enabled one, so a rename or extra tool fails the suite instead of silently widening the client contract.

`hypermnesic_search` is a pure alias: both it and `search` delegate to one shared `_search` closure, and a test asserts their advertised `outputSchema`s are identical; the alias exists for clients that auto-prefix tool names with the server id.

Every tool advertises an `outputSchema` generated from a `TypedDict` result model declared in the server module, and every input parameter carries a description; both properties are pinned by tests (parameter-schema and output-schema coverage).
Read tools are annotated `readOnlyHint: True` and the write tool `readOnlyHint: False`, giving a client a machine-readable statement of a tool's write capability before it calls anything.

Write-tool registration is per server, not per caller: the public OAuth `/mcp` lane (`build_cloud_server`) always builds write-enabled so every remote client sees `commit_note` in `tools/list` even with only the `read` scope, whose call is then refused; a tailnet read companion built with the default `write_enabled=False` (or `hypermnesic serve` without `--enable-write`) does not expose the tool at all.

A write-enabled serve bound to a tailnet address refuses to start without auth configured, with only a loopback bind or the explicit, CGNAT-bounded `--allow-tailnet-write` opt-in exempted, so on the network lanes a registered write tool implies a configured auth boundary.

Every read tool calls `_Backend.converge()` before its tool-specific query — search, the search alias, build_context, resolve, think, list_folders, and read_note alike — and convergence's outcome is returned as payload fields rather than raised as an error.

`_Backend` constructs the index, graph, and embedder lazily, and a missing or unusable embedding credential degrades the dense channel instead of failing server construction, so lexical and graph reads keep working with no key.

`search` reports `degraded_lexical_only` when either the query embedding or the convergence dense fill degraded, and prefers the convergence reason over the retrieval reason in `degraded_reason`; `think` merges the convergence reason into its own result.

`degraded_reason` names the provider or configuration state rather than just flagging failure: `missing_embedder` when no embedder was constructed, `configuration` for a rejected or missing credential, `rate_limited` for a provider 429, `cooldown` during the in-process cooldown that follows a 429, `api_error` for other provider statuses, and `embedding_error` as the fallback.

A provider 429 opens a cooldown (default 300 s, `EMBED_FAILURE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`) during which embedding calls are refused with reason `cooldown` while reads keep answering from lexical and graph evidence — documented client-facing behavior, not an outage.

`manual_reindex_recommended` is produced by convergence and is true only on the `oversized_delta` outcome, where the changed markdown delta between the index checkpoint and `HEAD` exceeds `CONVERGE_MAX_DELTA_FILES`; the read serves the current consistent projection and surfaces the signal instead of replaying inline.

Every read result carries `manual_reindex_recommended`; only `search` and `think` additionally carry the `degraded_lexical_only` / `degraded_reason` pair, while `build_context`, `resolve`, `list_folders`, and `read_note` do not.

Each `search` hit carries the repo-relative `path`, the matched `heading`, a rounded fused `score`, the sorted `channels` that matched it (`lexical`, `dense`, `doc`), a bounded snippet of at most 280 characters, and `recency` — the epoch seconds of the most recent commit touching that path, resolved from a single `git log` pass, or null when untracked.

`build_context(path, depth)` walks body `[[wikilinks]]` over both incoming and outgoing edges, is cycle-safe with a visited set, excludes the start page, and returns a sorted page-path list for reproducible results.

`resolve(name)` reuses the body-wikilink resolution rules (exact path, `.md` suffix, unambiguous stem, with `|display` alias and `#anchor` stripped) and returns `null` rather than guessing when a name is ambiguous or missing; `slug` is the returned path with `.md` stripped for use as a wikilink target.
`think` is read-only by construction — the module imports only read surfaces and cannot reach the write path — and `wrote: false` is the observable assertion of that boundary.

When `think`'s self-exclusion (the active note's `path`) removes every retrieval hit, it falls back to the note's explicit graph neighbourhood and returns those neighbours as low-confidence related notes with score 0.0 on the `graph` channel rather than a blank thinking surface.

Folder writability in `list_folders` is single-sourced with the write path: `build_server` computes the effective write surface once and shares it with `commit_note` and folder discovery, and each folder is classified by probing a synthetic note *under* its prefix through the write guard, so nested protected directories (e.g. `projects/scripts/`) are reported non-writable and `commit_note` refuses them too.

`list_folders` bounds its payload the same way convergence bounds a delta: entries are sorted before the node cap, truncation drops a deterministic tail and reports `truncated` with an `omitted` count, and the requested `depth` is clamped to a ceiling, so a large vault still returns a bounded answer the caller can drill into by narrowing `root`.

`list_folders` returns the requested root's direct instruction file only — `AGENTS.md` preferred, `CLAUDE.md` as fallback when `AGENTS.md` is absent at that same root — never aggregating descendant instruction files into a parent listing, and it sanitizes the content before returning it by replacing host-local absolute paths with `<local-path>` and private/tailnet endpoint URLs (including any `/mcp` URL) with `<endpoint-url>`.

An absolute or `..`-containing `root` for `list_folders` does not raise: the tool catches the rejection and returns an empty, leak-free listing with `agent_instruction: null`, so a malformed request cannot probe for out-of-vault paths through error messages.

`read_note`'s security boundary is index membership plus a resolved-within-repo check: only committed, in-vault markdown notes are in the index path set, so a `../` traversal, an absolute path, or a non-note file such as `.env` or anything under `.git/` returns `found: false` with `content: null` and never reads outside the vault.

`commit_note` self-enforces the `write` scope per call when auth is configured, because the transport's single global required-scope list cannot separate read clients from write clients on one endpoint; the refusal is actionable (reconnect and approve write access) and states that write approval does not bypass protected-path, frontmatter, dirty-tree, head-drift, audit, or git coordination guards.

On a server with no auth configured (loopback bind or the explicit tailnet-trust opt-in) there is no principal, so the write tool performs no scope check and the write-guard, frontmatter, drift, coordination, and audit controls are the only bound.

`commit_note`'s result is a union with four distinguishable branches: success (`committed: true` with `path`, `created`, `noop: false`, `new_sha`, `diff`), refusal (`committed: false` with `refused`), no-op (`committed: false` with `noop: true` and no new commit), and degraded success (`committed: true` with `index_degraded: true` and `degraded_reason`).

A refusal means nothing was written and no audit entry was created, while `index_degraded` means the commit landed and only its index projection failed — the caller must keep the returned SHA and must not rewrite the note elsewhere; the two are never conflated.

The write tool returns an explicit structured `CallToolResult` instead of a plain dict so FastMCP does not materialize absent union fields as nulls and reject them against the generated output schema; an HTTP regression test asserts a protected-path refusal reaches a remote client as a clean refusal payload rather than an output-validation error.

Refusals map the whole guard/gate/coordination exception set (`WriteGuardError`, `FrontmatterDriftError`, `HeadDriftError`, `DirtyTreeError`, `GitCoordinationError`, and gate input-shape `ValueError`) to `{committed: false, refused}`, so a remote client never receives a raw traceback in place of a control signal.

The tool descriptions are treated as part of the contract because they are the documentation an agent reads: they state that read tools converge first, that `resolve` returns null rather than guessing, that `think` never writes, that a degraded index means keep the SHA and do not rewrite the note, and that the search tools' retrieval model and return shape are lexical plus dense; tests assert the search descriptions stay substantive and self-identify the alias.

Changing the MCP tool surface is governed by the repository's non-negotiable documentation rule: adding, removing, or renaming a tool or changing its arguments requires `docs/reference/mcp-tools.md`, the tool list in `README.md`, and (when the serving picture moves) `ARCHITECTURE.md` in the same PR as the change.

The plugin SKILL may name only real engine tools, enforced by `tests/test_plugin.py`, so a renamed or removed engine tool that skips the plugin prose becomes a broken instruction for the agents reading it.
